record.file_problem: Repository README and file list only; code was not read or run, and no result files are listed.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports an Arditi-style mean-difference ablation attack and its refusal results, including a K=1 result on an unmodified instruct model. The study also extends the attack iteratively and tests training-time changes to its effectiveness.
record.gate_note: Results are reported in the README, so rows are recorded despite not reading or running the repository code. The README also reports sentiment results for GPT-2/IMDB, but those do not test refusal claims and are omitted. Probe accuracies, candidate-selection scores, and KL values used to choose attack directions are not reported as outcomes of the refusal ablation and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study reruns Arditi's difference-in-means ablation on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and finds one direction suffices (K=1). It extends the attack iteratively to the base model and to models trained with a matching+KD objective built to spread refusal across directions. These results bear on V1, V3 (the robustness-training clause), V4 and V7. The evidence is a README only; the preprint is not yet public.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that Cov L2+KD training spreads refusal so that iterated mean-difference ablation needs at least 16 directions, versus 1 for unmodified Instruct (≥16× attack rank). K=0 refusal stays near baseline (98/18 vs 100/15). Without KD, sentence-pool matching collapses behaviour, and pool alignment with the attacker's position matters. They also claim Cov L2+KD reorganises the linear structure rather than masking it (probe 0.991→0.955). Add that L1+KD raises harmless refusal to 43%.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an Arditi-style three-site ablation hook and mean-difference directions, but extends the attack by re-extracting and orthonormalizing directions iteratively. The main intervention is training-time mean/covariance matching plus KD rather than the original ablation-only study. Repository is a research tool/experiment repo; the README says the full evaluation is written up in a preprint to be linked once public.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes differ by training condition and pooling/KD setup: K=1 for unmodified Instruct, K=11 for L1 + KD, and at least K=16 for Cov L2 + KD; K=0 refusal behavior also differs across the sentence-pool, chat-template-pool, and KD conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: After Cov L2+KD training, a linear probe on the matched pool still classifies harmful versus harmless at 0.955 (from 0.991), even though single-direction ablation no longer removes refusal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmfulness stays linearly decodable after training spreads refusal so that no single direction ablates it (related to V4/V5, but probe accuracy is not a refusal rate).

record.problems: Evidence is reported only in the README; code and experiment outputs were not read or run. Refusal evaluations use 100 harmful and 100 harmless held-out prompts, and the README notes the 30% suppression threshold is rounded to absorb binomial sampling noise but gives no confidence intervals or other uncertainty estimates. General capability preservation is not evaluated for the refusal models.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the GPT-2/IMDB sentiment results because they concern sentiment rather than refusal. Omitted probe accuracies and attack candidate-scoring values because they do not directly report the refusal outcomes or attack threshold recorded here.

Whether natural jailbreaks act by suppressing the direction. Only an explicit linear-ablation attack is used.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence comes only from the README; code and outputs were not run, and the preprint is not public. The study covers one 1B model with 100/100 held-out prompts, one greedy seed, a WildGuard-7B judge and no confidence intervals. Suppression is defined as harmful refusal below 30%, not full removal. The attack's direction selection uses KL and induce-refusal filters taken from Arditi. The defense models are engineered to resist ablation, so the results on them are labelled limits_scope for V1 rather than challenges. The study is not among V1's original sources.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports refusal after ablation but not whether general capabilities remain intact. It does not report adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is evaluated.
The attack evaluated is an explicit linear-ablation attack, not an evaluation of naturally occurring jailbreaks. Robustness training is tested only through the reported ablation attack.
The README reports iterated ablation rank, but does not compare affine, cone, or other geometric models of refusal.
Harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are not separately measured.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages is evaluated as a transfer test.
The README compares some training conditions but does not systematically vary when refusal is trained or isolate training timing.
